Hi,

That seems a mypy bug, since the type allows for a `dict[str,str]`. I will try unioning the existing type with a `Mapping[str,str]` to see if mypy understands that

@CaselIT This is not a mypy bug: `Mapping` type is covariant in values, but not in keys. You can see https://github.com/python/typing/pull/273 and https://github.com/python/typing/issues/445 for some discussion.
So, for example, `Mapping[str, str | int]` is a super type of `Mapping[str, str]`, `Mapping[str | int, str]` is not. You may have to rewrite the type be a union of Mapping instead of a Mapping with a union of keys.
strange that pyright likes the current type, while mypy does not. Usually pyright is the correct one on complex types

    UniqueConstraint,
    CheckConstraint,
    ForeignKeyConstraint,
    PrimaryKeyConstraint,
]
_NamingSchemaCallable = Callable[[_AllConstraints, Table], str]
_NamingSchemaValue = Union[str, _NamingSchemaCallable]

_NamingSchemaParameter = Union[
    _NamingSchemaTD,
    Mapping[str, _NamingSchemaValue],
    Mapping[Type[_AllConstraints], _NamingSchemaValue],
    Mapping[Union[Type[_AllConstraints], str], _NamingSchemaValue],

that's a shame. as always python typing are quite lacking...

My workaround to silence the mypy error (until a proper fix is released):
```python
from sqlalchemy.sql.schema import _NamingSchemaTD

# use the convention that you have in your project
convention = _NamingSchemaTD(
    ix="ix_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_N_name)s",
    uq="uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_N_name)s",
    ck="ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
    fk="fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_N_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
    pk="pk_%(table_name)s",
)

metadata = sqlalchemy.MetaData(naming_convention=convention)
```

Defining it inline also works correctly
```py
import sqlalchemy as sa

metadata = sa.MetaData(
    naming_convention=dict(
        ix="ix_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_N_name)s",
        uq="uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_N_name)s",
        ck="ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
        fk="fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_N_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
        pk="pk_%(table_name)s",
    )
)

```

issue.title: naming convention docs refer to using classes as keys as well as callables for values in some cases; neither are typed

labels.name: schema
labels.description: things related to the DDL related objects like Table, Column, CreateIndex, etc.

labels.name: PRs (with tests!) welcome
labels.description: a fix or feature which is appropriate to be implemented by volunteers

issue.body:
### Ensure stubs packages are not installed

- [X] No sqlalchemy stub packages is installed (both `sqlalchemy-stubs` and `sqlalchemy2-stubs` are not compatible with v2)

### Verify if the api is typed

- [X] The api is not in a module listed in [#6810](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/6810) so it should pass type checking

### Describe the typing issue

The documentation on `MetaData.naming_convention` specifies that the keys of the mapping can be either string or a Constraint/Index type. However, [the type annotations](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/b95b22d8c0f9f26e33e1912d8ee205319fc20362/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/schema.py#L5088) only accept `Dict[str, str]`. Therefore, a dictionary with type `Dict[Type[Union[Constraint, Index]], str]` is not accepted.

As for the mapping values: it might probably need to accept a callable too for user token definitions, but I don't have this use case in my code.

### To Reproduce

```python
from typing import Dict, Type, Union

from sqlalchemy import MetaData
from sqlalchemy.sql.schema import (
    CheckConstraint,
    Constraint,
    ForeignKeyConstraint,
    Index,
    PrimaryKeyConstraint,
    UniqueConstraint,
)

naming_convention: Dict[Type[Union[Constraint, Index]], str] = {
    PrimaryKeyConstraint: "pk_%(table_name)s",
    ForeignKeyConstraint: "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
    CheckConstraint: "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
    UniqueConstraint: "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_N_name)s",
    Index: "ix_%(column_0_N_label)s",
}

metadata = MetaData(naming_convention=naming_convention)
```


### Error

```
<file>:<line>: error: Argument "naming_convention" to "MetaData" has incompatible type "Dict[Union[Type[Constraint], Type[Index]], str]"; expected "Optional[Dict[str, str]]"  [arg-type]
``` 

### Versions

- OS: **Debian 11.6**
- Python: **3.9.2**
- SQLAlchemy: **2.0.3**
- Type checker (eg: mypy 0.991, pyright 1.1.290, etc): **mypy 1.0.0**


### Additional context

_No response_

issue.title: chore(persistence): improve naming for indexes and constraints

labels.name: size:S
labels.description: This PR changes 10-29 lines, ignoring generated files.

issue.body:
- removes manual names for uniqueness constraints, which are redundant when using naming conventions and were actually conflicting with and overriding the naming conventions
- changes our naming conventions to better support compound indexes and compound uniqueness constraints (i.e., those that involve multiple columns)

Previously, if we created a compound index or uniqueness constrain, the automatically generated name would only include the first column, which makes naming collisions possible.

resolves #2975
